cards.design_implication: When simulating tidal evolution in differentially rotating binaries, one must acknowledge that this approach is an approximation that applies solid-body results shell-by-shell rather than a formally derived differential tidal theory.
does_not_establish: The physical accuracy of the tidal synchronization timescale compared to observational data.
The validity of the underlying physics of tides in differential rotation.
cards.evidence_excerpt: This extension of Hut’s work to diferentially rotating stars is not formally derived but merely applies his result for solid body rotators independently to each shell.
limitations: The text explicitly states the method is not formally derived.
Applicability is restricted to the specific numerical implementation in MESA.
cards.statement: The software implements tidal interactions by extending Hut's solid-body rotation model to differentially rotating stars, applying the result independently to each shell.

cards.design_implication: If strict numerical reproducibility across different hardware architectures is required for the design, this software property can be relied upon, whereas other tools may require platform-specific calibration.
does_not_establish: Reproducibility of results across different software codes or different parameter settings.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We close by noting that the MESA software infrastructure provides bit-for-bit consistency for all results across all the supported platforms
limitations: This claim applies to the software's numerical output given identical inputs and parameters.
It does not establish the scientific accuracy of the underlying physical models.
cards.statement: MESA software infrastructure provides bit-for-bit consistency for results across all supported platforms.

cards.design_implication: Study designs involving high-mass ratio transfers or very close separations must define a termination criterion that avoids entering common envelope or contact states, or use an external method to handle these phases.
does_not_establish: The physical conditions that define the onset of common envelope evolution in reality.
Alternative methods for handling these phases.
cards.evidence_excerpt: MESA cannot model common envelope or contact binaries.
limitations: This is a capability limitation of the specific software module described.
cards.statement: The binary evolution module explicitly excludes the modeling of common envelope and contact binary phases.

cards.design_implication: For simulations requiring precise tracking of mass transfer rates (dot M_RLOF) to avoid large numerical jumps, implicit bisection-based root solves should be configured rather than explicit schemes.
does_not_establish: The absolute accuracy of these rates compared to 3D hydrodynamical simulations.
cards.evidence_excerpt: if one needs accurate values of $\dot { M } _ { \mathrm { R L O F } }$ and stellar radius, this requires use of an implicit scheme.
limitations: Implicit schemes may require more computational overhead per step than explicit schemes.
Depends on the choice of tolerance parameter (xi).
cards.statement: Implicit mass transfer schemes are used to compute mass transfer rates and stellar radii accurately, particularly when no closed-form formula is available.
